17 The diagram shows three cargo ships, \(A,B\) and \(C\), which are in the same horizontal plane. Ship \(B\) is 50 km due north of ship \(A\) and ship \(C\) is 70 km from ship \(A\). The bearing of \(C\) from \(A\) is \(020^\circ\).\par a Calculate the distance between ships \(B\) and \(C\), in kilometres to 3 s.f. (3 marks)\par b Calculate the bearing of ship \(C\) from ship \(B\). (4 marks)

\textbf{a}\[\begin{aligned}a^2&=b^2+c^2-2bc\cos A\\a^2&=70^2+50^2-2\times70\times50\cos20^\circ\\a^2&=4900+2500-6577.848\ldots\\a^2&=822.15165\ldots\end{aligned}\]So \(a=28.673\ldots\).\par So the distance between ships \(B\) and \(C\) is 28.7 km (3 s.f.).

\textbf{b}\[\begin{aligned}\cos B&=\frac{a^2+c^2-b^2}{2ac}\\\cos B&=\frac{28.673^2+50^2-70^2}{2(28.673)(50)}\\\cos B&=\frac{822.15165+2500-4900}{2867.3187}\\\cos B&=-0.55028\ldots\\B&=\cos^{-1}0.55028\ldots\\&=123.3867\ldots^\circ\end{aligned}\]The bearing is \(180^\circ-123.3867^\circ=56.6^\circ\). So the bearing of ship \(C\) from ship \(B\) is \(056.6^\circ\).

11 In \(\triangle ABC\), \(AB=x\text{ cm}, BC=(4-x)\text{ cm}, \angle BAC=y\) and \(\angle BCA=30^\circ\).\par Given that \(\sin y=\frac1{\sqrt2}\), show that

Using \(\frac a{\sin A}=\frac c{\sin C}\)\[\Rightarrow\frac{4-x}{\sin y^\circ}=\frac x{\sin30^\circ}\]\[\Rightarrow(4-x)\sin30^\circ=x\sin y^\circ\]\[\Rightarrow(4-x)\times\tfrac12=x\times\frac1{\sqrt2}\]Multiply throughout by 2:\[\begin{aligned}4-x&=x\sqrt2\\x+\sqrt2x&=4\\x(1+\sqrt2)&=4\\x&=\frac4{1+\sqrt2}\end{aligned}\]
Multiply 'top and bottom' by \(\sqrt2-1\):\[\begin{aligned}x&=\frac{4(\sqrt2-1)}{(\sqrt2-1)(\sqrt2+1)}\\&=\frac{4(\sqrt2-1)}{2-1}\\&=4(\sqrt2-1)\end{aligned}\]

blocks.tex: 4 Triangle \(ABC\) is such that \(AB=4\text{ cm},BC=6\text{ cm}\) and \(\angle ACB=36^\circ\). Show that one of the possible values of \(\angle ABC\) is \(25.8^\circ\) (to 3 s.f.). Using this value, calculate the length of \(AC\).

As \(4<6,36^\circ<\angle BAC\), so there are two possible values for angle \(A\).\par Using \(\frac{\sin A}a=\frac{\sin C}c\)\[\frac{\sin A}6=\frac{\sin36^\circ}4,\qquad\sin A=\frac{6\sin36^\circ}4\]\[A=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{6\sin36^\circ}4\right)\text{ or }A=180^\circ-\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{6\sin36^\circ}4\right)\]\[A=61.845\ldots^\circ\text{ or }A=118.154\ldots^\circ\]When \(A=118.154\ldots^\circ\):\[\angle ABC=180^\circ-(36^\circ+118.154\ldots^\circ)=25.8^\circ\text{ (3 s.f.)}\]

Using this value for \(\angle ABC\) with\[\frac b{\sin B}=\frac c{\sin C},\qquad\frac{AC}{\sin25.8^\circ}=\frac4{\sin36^\circ}\]\[\text{So }AC=\frac{4\sin25.8^\circ}{\sin36^\circ}=2.96\text{ cm (3 s.f.)}\]

blocks.tex: 4 In triangle \(ABC,BC=(x+2)\text{ cm},AC=x\text{ cm}\) and \(\angle BCA=150^\circ\). Given that the area of the triangle is \(5\text{ cm}^2\), work out the value of \(x\), giving your answer to 3 significant figures.

Area of \(\triangle ABC=\frac12x(x+2)\sin150^\circ\text{ cm}^2\).\[\begin{aligned}\text{So }5&=\tfrac12x(x+2)\times\tfrac12\\\text{So }20&=x(x+2)\\\Rightarrow x^2+2x-20&=0\end{aligned}\]Using the quadratic formula:\[x=\frac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}\]\[x=\frac{-2\pm\sqrt{84}}2\]\(x=3.582\ldots\) or \(x=-5.582\ldots\).\par As \(x>0,x=3.58\) (3 s.f.).

blocks.tex: 12 The perimeter of \(\triangle ABC=15\text{ cm}\). Given that \(AB=7\text{ cm}\) and \(\angle BAC=60^\circ\), find the lengths of \(AC\) and \(BC\) and the area of the triangle.

Using the cosine rule\[a^2=b^2+c^2-2bc\cos A\]with \(a=x,b=(8-x),c=7\) and \(A=60^\circ\).\[\begin{aligned}x^2&=(8-x)^2+49-2(8-x)\times7\times\cos60^\circ\\x^2&=64-16x+x^2+49-7(8-x)\\x^2&=64-16x+x^2+49-56+7x\\\Rightarrow9x&=57\\\Rightarrow x&=\tfrac{57}9=\tfrac{19}3=6\tfrac13\end{aligned}\]

So \(BC=6\frac13\text{ cm}\) and\[AC=(8-6\tfrac13)\text{ cm}=1\tfrac23\text{ cm}\]\[\begin{aligned}\text{Area}&=\tfrac12bc\sin A\\&=\tfrac12\times7\times\tfrac53\times\sin60^\circ\\&=5.0518\ldots\\&=5.05\text{ cm}^2\text{ (3 s.f.)}\end{aligned}\]

blocks.tex: (i) The volume of \(OABC=\frac13\times\) the area of triangle \(OAB\times OC=\frac16abc\).\par(ii) Using the scalar product with vectors \(\overrightarrow{CA}\) and \(\overrightarrow{CB}\),\[\sqrt{a^2+c^2}\sqrt{b^2+c^2}\times\cos\theta=\begin{pmatrix}a\\0\\-c\end{pmatrix}\cdot\begin{pmatrix}0\\b\\-c\end{pmatrix}=c^2\Rightarrow\cos\theta=\frac{c^2}{\sqrt{a^2+c^2}\sqrt{b^2+c^2}}\]The cosine rule \((AB^2=AC^2+BC^2-2\times AC\times BC\times\cos\theta)\) will also yield this result.\par The area of triangle \(ABC\) will be \(\frac12\times\sqrt{a^2+c^2}\sqrt{b^2+c^2}\times\sin\theta\)\[\begin{aligned}&=\frac12\times\sqrt{a^2+c^2}\sqrt{b^2+c^2}\times\sqrt{1-\left(\frac{c^2}{\sqrt{a^2+c^2}\sqrt{b^2+c^2}}\right)^2}\quad\text{(because }\sin^2\theta=1-\cos^2\theta)\\&=\frac12\times\sqrt{(a^2+c^2)(b^2+c^2)-c^4}\\&=\frac12\times\sqrt{a^2b^2+b^2c^2+c^2a^2}\end{aligned}\]So \[\frac13\times\left(\frac12\times\sqrt{a^2b^2+b^2c^2+c^2a^2}\right)\times d=\frac16abc\Rightarrow\frac1{d^2}=\frac{a^2b^2+b^2c^2+c^2a^2}{a^2b^2c^2}\]which simplifies to the stated result.\par A similar result is true for the right-angled triangle \(PQR\), in which \(X\) is the foot of the perpendicular from the right-angle \(Q\) to the hypotenuse \(PR\): \(\frac1{PQ^2}+\frac1{QR^2}=\frac1{QX^2}\).
